summary: Abridgment of 'The Dynamo and the Virgin (1900)' that keeps all eight verbatim excerpts and the plan's essential chain: Langley's tour, Bacon, and Chicago 1893; the dynamo as moral force; the steam/current fracture; the historian's broken neck; 310 and Constantine; translating rays into faith; Virgin/Venus as force against sexless America; St. Gaudens at Amiens with Gibbon; Chartres; and the scholastic thicket and the pen before the Cherbourg sailing.
acceptable_changes: Added 'of the Smithsonian' to Langley's first mention, per the plan's dependency instruction, so the surname is not orphaned.
Cut King James I. Kept the Marx sentence for the Berlin dependency. Reduced the tram and locomotive details to the steam-engine clause.
Reduced the Marconi, Branly, frozen air and electric furnace material to the single Branly-coherer question.
Cut the Dante Italian tercet and its framing sentence. Kept the Lucretius Latin line and the explicit Lucretius/Venus, Dante/Virgin comparison.
Compressed St. Gaudens's character list and the Mont Parnasse/Bois outings. Kept 'most inarticulate,' no egoist, and his illness that summer.
Cut Isis at Edfoo, Louis XI, Cnidos/Aphrodite and the Matthew Arnold comparison. The railway-train sentence now has 'Artists' as its subject because Arnold was cut.

Shortened the Zeno-to-Pascal list to two names. Condensed the mathematicians' convenience passage to the compass-needle sentence. Trimmed the pen/crystallization passage to the blind-man's dog and 'struck out' lines.
risks: The Lucretius line is kept in Latin without a gloss, which is one of the two options the plan allows. Readers without Latin get the meaning only from the Venus/Virgin framing.
The section balance is approximate. No count was measured.
review_focus: The 'Artists felt a railway train as power' bridge, which replaces the cut Arnold/St. Gaudens subject.
The 'St. Gaudens let Adams go about in his company' compression, which joins two source paragraphs.
